answer: Harbor law caps registered berths to the slips a municipal jetty can physically host, each leased to one signing key. The lease plaque is a unique mineral pigment fused into a numbered timber pile at that slip. Inspectors core the pile, match the grain to the public registry, and demand a signature over a fresh nonce from the bound key. A second claimant on the same pile forfeits the bond. Forging a hundred identities means buying a hundred scarce slips and driving a hundred uniquely assayed piles, each paid for and physically installed.
